prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
competitors_mentioned: Rescue Rooter and One Hour Heating
Require a Manual J Load Calculation
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your exact location, home size, budget, equipment preference, and how important warranty/response time is to you. If you share your Atlanta ZIP code and a few preferences (budget, brand you want, timeline), I can pull a short list of highly rated local companies and recent reviews.

How to pick the best company for your AC replacement
- Check credentials: current Georgia business license/registration if required, proof of insurance, and EPA 608 certification for refrigerant handling. NATE‑certified technicians are a good sign.
- Confirm experience: ask how many years they’ve been installing central AC in Atlanta and request local references.
- Require a Manual J load calculation and Manual S equipment selection: sizing matters — an oversized or undersized replacement wastes money and shortens equipment life.
- Compare written bids: include equipment brand/model and SEER rating, labor, permit fees, ductwork changes, thermostat type, removal/disposal, and start/finish dates.
- Warranty & guarantees: get both manufacturer and installer warranties in writing. Ask about labor warranties and what’s covered.
- Permits and inspections: a reputable contractor pulls required permits and arranges inspections.
- Financing & rebates: ask about financing, local utility or Georgia power rebates, and federal tax credits (if applicable).
- Read reviews and check complaints: Google, Yelp, Angi, and the Better Business Bureau for patterns over time, not just one review.

Practical checklist of questions to ask each contractor
1. Are you licensed, insured, and EPA 608 certified? Can you show proof?
2. Will you perform a Manual J load calculation and provide the report?
3. What brand, model, and SEER rating are you proposing? Can I review the spec sheet?
4. What exactly is included in the price (duct work, new thermostat, permits, disposal)?
5. What are the manufacturer and labor warranties? Is labor warranty written?
6. Who does the warranty work — you or a third party?
7. Do you have local references? Can I see recent online reviews?
8. When can you start, and how long will the job take?
9. Do you offer financing or know of local rebates?

Rough cost range (Atlanta, typical single‑family home)
- Expect central AC replacement to commonly fall somewhere around $3,500–$10,000 depending on tonnage, SEER, ductwork, and complexity. Get multiple bids before deciding.

Reputable names in the Atlanta area
- Some well‑known contractors that serve Atlanta include Coolray (regional), Moncrief Heating & Air Conditioning (GA-based), and national/local franchise branches like ARS/Rescue Rooter and One Hour Heating & Air. These are examples — I can produce an up‑to‑date, ranked list of top-rated local firms in your neighborhood if you give your ZIP code.
